steps.title: Genetic Variation
steps.body: Variation exists between individuals of the same species due to genetic and environmental factors. Mutations create new alleles. Genetic engineering and selective breeding allow humans to modify organisms for specific purposes.

steps.title: Variation
steps.body: Differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species. Variation can be caused by genetic factors, environmental factors, or a combination of both.

steps.title: Continuous vs discontinuous variation
steps.body: Continuous: A range of values with no distinct categories (e.g. height, weight). Usually influenced by many genes and the environment. Shown as a line graph or histogram. Discontinuous: Distinct categories with no in-between values (e.g. blood group A/B/AB/O, eye colour). Usually controlled by a single gene. Shown as a bar chart.

steps.title: Mutation
steps.body: A change in the DNA sequence of a gene. Mutations happen spontaneously (randomly) and continuously. Most mutations have no effect on the organism.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Continuous variation = range (like a bell curve); discontinuous = distinct categories (like bar chart) Most mutations have NO effect — don't say "all mutations are harmful" Learn the genetic engineering steps in order and name the enzymes: restriction enzyme to CUT, ligase to JOIN The plasmid is the VECTOR — it carries the gene into the bacterium When discussing GM crops, always give balanced arguments (advantages AND disadvantages) Selective breeding is SLOW (many generations); genetic engineering is FASTER (direct gene transfer) Selective breeding reduces the gene pool — this is a key disadvantage to remember Don't confuse genetic engineering (transferring genes between species) with selective breeding (choosing parents within the same species)
